title: Design system pattern ledger
description: The record of what the design system allows, what each pattern means, and how mature each one is. Not a class table: a ledger. The library mapping is the part expected to change; the intent is the part that must not.

version.description: Schema version. Bump when the shape changes so the verifier can refuse a file it does not understand.

libraries.description: Libraries this ledger knows how to emit for. A pattern does not have to map to all of them; a missing mapping means 'this library cannot express this pattern', which is itself worth recording.

components.description: One entry per component the design system has an opinion about. A component absent from here is ungoverned — the verifier says nothing about it.

intent.description: What this component is for, in plain language. Read by a human deciding whether to add a pattern, and by an agent deciding whether a request belongs here at all.

namespace.description: Per library, a regular expression matching every class that belongs to this component. This is what makes the ledger an ALLOWLIST: a class matching the namespace that no allowed pattern produces is a violation, even if nobody wrote a forbidden entry for it. Without this the ledger could only catch mistakes someone predicted.

modifiers.description: Orthogonal axes that combine with any pattern (size, width). Kept separate from patterns so the ledger does not have to enumerate the cross product — which is exactly how a vocabulary reaches 500 variations without anyone deciding to.

patterns.description: The vocabulary. Every key here is a name application code and agents may use.

namespaceNote.description: Why the namespace regex is drawn where it is. A prefix is rarely exactly one component.

root.description: Per library, a regex matching the class that MAKES an element this component. Optional, and only needed when a library shares modifier classes across components: Bulma's `is-fullwidth` belongs to buttons, selects, tags and files alike, so a namespace alone would claim it wherever it appears. With `root` declared, the namespace is only consulted on elements that actually are this component. Defaults to `namespace`, which is right for libraries like Bootstrap whose prefixes are unambiguous.

docs.description: Where to send a reader for everything this ledger does NOT redocument.

library.description: URL of the library's own documentation for this component.

options.description: Allowed values for this axis, each mapping to per-library classes. An empty class list means 'this is the default and adds nothing'.

forbidden.description: Values deliberately removed from this axis.

intent.description: What this pattern MEANS, independent of any library. This is the load-bearing field. If the project swaps Bootstrap for something else, or the library renames a class, the intent is what lets an agent rebuild the mapping instead of guessing from class names.

state.description: Maturity, and the instruction to the agent. `raw` emit library classes. `styled` emit the project's semantic class over a library component. `own` emit the project's class for a component the library does not have — built from tokens, with nothing underneath. `wrapped` emit the framework component. `forbidden` refuse and offer the alternative. Promotion is: fill the next slot, then change this field. `own` is not a rung on that ladder — it is a parallel origin, and a component that starts there never had a library composition to be promoted from.

raw.description: Library classes, per library. Present from day one; it is the scaffolding.

styled.description: The project's own semantic class. Used by both `styled` and `own`: the class is the same shape either way, and what differs is whether a library component sits underneath it.

wrapped.description: The framework component, once one exists. It should render the `styled` class, not the library composition — that is what keeps the wrapper thin and makes removing the library a one-file change.

reason.description: Required when state is `forbidden`. Why this is not in the vocabulary. A refusal without a reason gets overridden by the next person in a hurry.

instead.description: The pattern to use in its place. A refusal that does not name an alternative just moves the problem.

matches.description: For forbidden patterns: the library classes that indicate someone reached for this, so the verifier can name it precisely instead of reporting an anonymous unknown class.

example.description: A minimal markup snippet showing the pattern in use. Read by the documentation generator, which renders it live next to the source — a docs page whose examples are screenshots goes stale without anyone noticing. Required in practice for anything a reader cannot look up in the library's own docs.

parts.description: For a COMPOSITION: the element classes it is made of, each with what it holds. A composition is the only place these are written down, since the library has no such component — so the ledger has to carry the anatomy that `namespaceNote` otherwise leaves to the library.

diverges.description: For an OVERRIDE: what this changes about the library's component, and why. The documentation generator prints exactly this and links the rest to the library's docs, which is what keeps the page a delta rather than a second catalogue.

libraryClasses.description: Library name to the exact class list for that library.
